key_insight: A monolayer graphene front contact improves current collection and fill factor in AlInN/Si solar cells without significantly changing open-circuit voltage.
engineering_relevance: Graphene offers a low-temperature transparent conductive contact that can boost nitride-based photovoltaic performance while remaining compatible with semiconductor device integration.
method: Grow AlxIn1-xN (x = 0.22, 0.35, 0.43) on p-type Si(100) with a thin a-Si buffer layer.
Transfer a monolayer graphene film onto the front surface as a semitransparent conductive contact.
Compare illuminated and dark photovoltaic behavior for devices with and without graphene.
evidence_signal: Across all three Al compositions, graphene-enhanced devices showed higher short-circuit current density, fill factor, and power conversion efficiency, while Voc stayed largely unchanged.
watch_item: The benefit depends on reliable large-area graphene transfer and low-resistance contact quality, which may introduce process variability.
paper_title: Enhancement of nitride-based solar cells using graphene as transparent contact layer
